notes: v1.14.589 - IMAGE INPUT FOR THE DCT ASSISTANT. A technician can attach a photo to a question and get an answer. Five phases of phantom-image-input-plan.md, landing together. The existing .txt/.log/.json/.eml/.csv import is UNCHANGED - the image path branches around it at the top of va_importTicket and returns, and nothing below that line was edited or reordered.  WHAT A TECHNICIAN SEES: IMPORT FILE now offers photos as well as text files. Picking one attaches it with a PHOTO ATTACHED chip showing size and dimensions, the next question carries it, and the answer comes back as usual. Clearing the chip or closing the sheet drops it.  THE CEILING IS THE DESIGN. phantomAPI refuses a body over PHANTOM_API_MAX_BODY (300,000) BEFORE the network and base64 inflates a blob by 4/3, so a fixed compression setting cannot work. The plan asked for 1600px @ 0.80 targeting 400 KB; measured, that is 533 KB base64 - nearly double a limit that already existed - and even the app's existing 1280/0.70 default produced 271,259 bytes from a noisy 3000x2000 JPEG. So va_prepareImage walks a ladder (1280/.70, 1024/.65, 800/.60, 640/.55) and takes the first rung that fits, and the budget it fits is MEASURED AT SEND TIME from the real request envelope - not a constant, because the system prompt also carries buildContext, brief_buildLiveContext, hwMatrix_queryContext and a ticket capped at 12,000 chars. If the photo prepared at import no longer fits, it is re-prepared FROM THE ORIGINAL FILE, never from the already-lossy copy.  ONE COMPRESSOR, NOT TWO. The plan asked for a new compressImage(); photo_compress (used by rack photo capture) already did that work, so it was PARAMETERISED instead - Contract A2, one canonical engine per concept. Its defaults are the old hard-coded 1280/0.70, so photo_handleCapture, which passes neither argument, is served byte-identically. That function had ZERO test coverage before this ship; its default behaviour is now pinned.  NO NEW STORAGE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The plan's Phase 4 assumed conversation state lived in localStorage and that images had to be diverted into IndexedDB. The assistant persists NO conversation at all - VA is in-memory and dies with the sheet - so there was nothing to divert and no store to build. Building one would have been a third photo database beside phantom-attachments and phantom-photos. Phase 4 shipped the GUARD instead: tests that fail the day a photo reaches localStorage, because base64 photos there would exhaust the quota and take saved work with them.  NO SILENT FAILURES. A photo that cannot be decoded, or cannot fit even at the smallest rung, returns null and says so with a warn and a toast. A size refusal at send time is named as a SIZE problem - without that branch it would have surfaced as "Could not reach assistant" and sent a technician to check their signal over something they can fix by clearing the attached ticket.  TWO DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED DURING THE WORK: va_prepareImage treated a budget of 0 as "use the default", so a caller computing a genuinely-zero remaining budget silently got a generous one and a photo that could never send. And photo_encodeImage did not release its canvas backing store - a 12MP canvas is tens of megabytes and the ladder can build four, which is the difference on a phone between a decode that succeeds and one that returns empty; it now frees it win or lose.  PINNED by test/e2e/58-assistant-import-file.spec.js (5, the anti-breakage tripwire), 59-image-compression.spec.js (7), 60-image-input-flag.spec.js (5), 61-image-storage-safety.spec.js (5) and 62-image-send-budget.spec.js (5). 27 passed together.  NOT IN THIS SHIP: camera capture (Phase 6, one attribute, deliberately last), and alpha flattening - a transparent PNG still comes back as JPEG, deferred by owner ruling.  DEVICE VERIFY OWED: IMPORT FILE offers photos; pick one from the library and confirm the PHOTO ATTACHED chip shows size and dimensions; ask a question and confirm an answer returns; confirm a .log import still behaves exactly as before; confirm the card subtitle ".txt · .log · .json · .csv · PHOTO" does not wrap badly at 390px.
